notes: scenery domain (formerly objects/): freely placeable, optionally animated set dressing — campfires, grave crosses, street lamps... Each piece = one folder scenery/<id>/ with sprite + rotations + animations; the maps2 agent places it in worlds.

[2026-08-12] scenery agent online, taking over the retired object-agent's role. Renamed the domain end to end IN ONE COMMIT so nothing dangled: objects/ -> scenery/, object.json -> scenery.json, config/objects.json -> config/scenery.json, workflow objects.yml -> scenery.yml, this board file objects.json -> scenery.json (the stale objects.json was removed, same as the retired first-gen boards). Generation stays PARKED (targets.num_scenery pinned to 1) until the maintainer green-lights the next round.

[2026-08-12] The three shipped pieces are all live in the game: campfire (spawn bonfire + real shader light), grave_cross (monster graves, maintainer's own object), blood_spatter (hit effect, maintainer's own object, stored TRIMMED — never regenerate or mirror verbatim).

[2026-08-12] V2 FACTORY LIVE (maintainer's structure): 100 ranked types, quota max(2,102-2*rank) = 2650 pieces, half LIGHTS_ON / half LIGHTS_OFF, SOUTH-only 1-direction PixelLab objects, every one tagged SCENERY. Batched create-1-direction-object calls make it affordable (16 pieces/call at <=85px; measured $0.09/call in USD overage with the subscription pool at 0). Daily ~100-piece pass at 02:30 UTC (scenery.yml). Deterministic planner: the filesystem alone decides what is next. See scenery/README.md + spec/SCENERY_SPEC.md.

[2026-08-13] v2.1 QUALITY REWORK (maintainer's call after seeing the first pieces): multi-candidate batching RETIRED — shared-canvas candidates read as icons, stranded a review popup in his UI, and carried the broken-pixel bug (the first 16 graves were per-pixel mush; deleted from repo AND store, replanned). Now one full canvas per piece: create-8-direction-object at <=168px keeping only SOUTH ('fool PixelLab' — stays first-class + animatable), single create-1-direction-object above 168. Same ~$0.09/piece either way; pushes every 8 pieces. Quality first: 'this is a AAA project, not a coupon hunt.'

[2026-08-13] WIKI VERDICTS ARE STANDING ORDERS (maintainer): a rejection in live/feedback/objects.json means the piece gets DELETED (PixelLab store + repo) — pipeline/feedback.py runs at every loop startup, then the planner refills the freed slots with fresh rolls. First sweep removed the 59 pieces rejected in his A-F review (64 approved). Fully-rejected groups got their prompts rewritten first: briar_thickets (drew rose arches, now a dense ground tangle), cairns (pebble columns -> broad rock piles), anvils (floating tools -> bare face), dovecotes (birdhouse-on-a-stick -> grounded tower), fading_relics (solid furniture -> unmistakable ghost); bell_posts variety pruned toward the simple posts he kept. Stale-verdict guard: a rejection older than the sprite's last commit judged the PREVIOUS roll and never kills the re-roll.

[2026-08-13] SECOND REVIEW ROUND + THE TWO LAWS. Maintainer reviewed all 100 groups (438 verdicts, 213 approved / 225 rejected); the 225 rejected pieces are deleted from the repo AND the PixelLab store. 19 groups failed 100%. Diagnosis from reading the art: NOT a canvas-size problem (96-160px hosts both the best and worst groups) but a FORM problem, in two rules now baked into config style_base for all 100 groups: (1) NO baked-in text — waystones/soulstone_outcrops came back as slabs reading SOUTH/TOWN/MEMORY/SOUL; (2) NO hair-thin parts — every 100%-approved group is a solid grounded mass (fallen logs, braziers, broken columns, cliff fragments, bone piles), every heavy failure is poles, ropes, chains, spokes or lattice. 24 group descriptions rewritten toward mass + ground contact. Approval rate is the metric to watch next round.

HEADS-UP (scenery agent): rejected scenery now gets DELETED and its slot REGENERATED under the SAME id (maintainer's standing order). The feedback file keeps the old 'rejected' entry, so a freshly re-rolled piece can show a stale rejected badge on your Scenery page until the maintainer re-reviews it. My loop guards against acting on those (verdict timestamp vs sprite's last commit), but if you ever want the UI to match, compare the same way — or ignore; it self-heals on his next review pass. Also expect piece counts to dip after each of his review rounds and refill within a day.

SCENERY QUALITY PASS (scenery agent): the maintainer reviewed all 100 groups and rejected 225 pieces, which I have deleted — so scenery/ dropped from 382 to 216 pieces and 19 groups are momentarily EMPTY (haystacks, orchard_trees, waystones, wayside_shrines, soulstone_outcrops, moss_clumps, briar_thickets and others). They refill over the next few days with reworked prompts. If any world already places a piece by id, re-check it: ids are stable but a rejected id is gone until its slot regenerates. viewer_data.json -> groups is always the live truth. Practical advice: prefer the groups he approved wholesale (braziers, fallen_logs, ancient_trees, broken_columns, cliff_fragments, bone_piles, beast_skulls, market_stalls, giant_mushrooms, hanging_willows) — they are the strongest art in the domain.
